clue.text: More ready for a screw?

parts.note: taken as written
screw is British prison slang for a warder or guard

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is keener on a screw, whether the tool or something ruder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' tempts a tool or a sexual reading; here it is British prison slang for a warder.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward means ready or eager, so the comparative form means more ready or keener.

clue.text: Sports organisation raises cap to Middle East party

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A sporting body lifts its headgear in salute to a Middle Eastern political party.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'raises' reads the hat word from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatah is the Palestinian political faction founded by Yasser Arafat, a party in the Middle East.

clue.text: Unusual coin for sustenance in Wales

parts.note: rare means unusual
a bit is an old word for a small coin, as in threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A rare coin is what keeps someone going in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast, hence its link to Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a traditional cheese-on-toast dish, so it is food eaten in Wales.

clue.text: A study of port

parts.note: a den is a small private room for work or study

explanation.surface: A piece of research on a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport city in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Sad type died, with appropriate prayer

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
RIP, rest in peace, is the prayer fitting for the dead

explanation.surface: A gloomy person passed away and was given a fitting prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP is apt after 'died', which is why the clue calls the prayer appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is informal for a feeble, dull or wet person, a sad type.

clue.text: Regret baggy state of jumper, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: a jumper is a kangaroo, a roo, and its baggy pouch shows fullness

explanation.surface: Someone laments how their knitted sweater has stretched and gone baggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a British sweater but is a kangaroo (roo); 'roo fullness' spoken matches the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruefulness is sorrowful regret, the feeling of being sorry for something done.

clue.text: Last of 9 about 4, possibly

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the number may be arranged another way

parts.note: the figure written as the word four

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like instruction about the last item in a list of nine, near the fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to 9 across, whose last word is ISLAND, so the definition is any island; '4' is the number written out.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, so it fits the final word of 9 across.

clue.text: So careless, breaking the dishes

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of the phrase are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone so clumsy that they are smashing the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Casseroles are cooking pots and the stews cooked in them, both dishes.

clue.text: Colour is said to provide cash

indicators.note: said shows the words are spoken and their sound gives the entry

parts.note: red is a colour, followed by is

explanation.surface: Someone claims a colour will supply money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red is' spoken sounds like the slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is British slang for ready money, banknotes or cash in hand.

clue.text: It's beneath Macbeth perhaps, to put it mildly

parts.note: under means beneath
Macbeth is an example of a play, by Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Something lies below Shakespeare's tragedy, to say the least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put it mildly' looks like a comment but is the definition, a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To underplay something is to present it with restraint, downplaying or understating it.

clue.text: League is light source of unwelcome reaction

parts.note: a league is an old measure of three miles
to light on is to alight or land

explanation.surface: A sports league is a bright source of an unpleasant response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaction' means a nuclear reaction: Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania suffered a partial meltdown in 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: Three Mile Island was the site of the 1979 US nuclear accident, an infamous nuclear plant.

clue.text: Potboilers philosopher uttered

indicators.note: uttered means the name is spoken and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: Thomas Hobbes was the English philosopher who wrote Leviathan

explanation.surface: A thinker spoke of hack writing produced just for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potboilers' suggests hack novels, but read literally it means things that boil pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobs are the cooking rings on a stove, which heat pans and so boil pots.

clue.text: Above the lake

definitions.meaning: the largest of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.definitionFit: Superior means higher or better than, and Lake Superior is the greatest of the Great Lakes.

clue.text: Treating one — a way to gain favour

indicators.note: way hints that the letters go a different way, rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Treating someone is a way to win their approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals the rearranging of TREATING, I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingratiate oneself is to work to win someone's goodwill or favour.

clue.text: Perhaps London's galleries are as Venice or Florence once were

definitions.text: as Venice or Florence once were

parts.note: London is an example of a city, and the possessive gives an s
the Tates are London's art galleries, such as Tate Modern and Tate Britain

explanation.surface: London's art galleries are said to resemble Renaissance Italian republics.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE galleries are well known in London; the definition describes self-governing Italian republics.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice and Florence were independent republics governing a city and its territory, sovereign city states.

clue.text: Gnarled tree not in keeping

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A twisted tree that is not being kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to something, keeping it.

clue.text: They may be taken lying down

definitions.text: They may be taken lying down

parts.words: They may be taken lying down
parts.note: suggests something accepted meekly, but literally treatments followed while lying in bed

explanation.definitionFit: Rest cures are medical treatments of prolonged bed rest, so patients take them lying down.

clue.text: Bird on the river line

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, with several of that name

explanation.surface: A bird sits on the river line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, one flowing through York.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a blackbird or the ring ouzel, a thrush.

clue.text: Like the sunrise over Leatherhead

indicators.note: over says the climbing word covers or arches over what follows

parts.note: to soar is to rise high
the head, or first letter, of Leather

explanation.surface: A sunrise seen over the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunrise' splits into 'sun' and 'rise'; Leatherhead is a real town in Surrey, but here it gives L, the head of 'Leather'.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means of or relating to the sun.

clue.text: Look at soldier's state, not without reason

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a GI is an American soldier
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a soldier's homeland with good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical means rational or reasoned, so it is not lacking in reason.

clue.text: Strayed off after the old time

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the archaic article

parts.note: ye is the old way of writing the

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone astray, out of order

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off after an old period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' is a crossword convention: YE is a mock-archaic spelling of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday means the day before today, or times past generally.

clue.text: It's fitting enclosure between last month and start of year

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the year's last month
enc is an abbreviation for enclosure, as on a letter

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of year

explanation.surface: A suitable fenced space between December and the new year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' only describes where the enclosure sits, between the month and the year's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Decency is proper, seemly behaviour, the quality of being fitting.

clue.text: Think of building one cottage

indicators.note: building means the letters are constructed afresh into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone muses about building a cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply or ponder.

clue.text: Dicks after a drug

indicators.note: after puts the detectives behind the a

parts.note: dicks is slang for detectives, and the CID is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Detectives are chasing a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for the hallucinogenic drug LSD.

clue.text: Adder may give rise to terror

indicators.note: may give rise to says the snake's letters can produce a different word

explanation.surface: A venomous snake may cause fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or terror.

clue.text: It's somewhat over a trifle athletic!

definitions.text: It's somewhat over a trifle athletic!

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Something is rather more than a little athletic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'trifle athletic'; the whole clue describes a famously high-jumping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny insect that can leap many times its own body length, impressively athletic.

clue.text: Component to raise catch

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a part is a component

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a piece of machinery to grab something.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a device to catch animals, and to trap is to catch.

clue.text: A clear article on mending social attitude

indicators.note: mending suggests broken parts are put back together, here letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A clear newspaper article on repairing social views.
explanation.definitionFit: Racial tolerance is acceptance of people of all races, a social attitude.

clue.text: Crackpot loves to do this!

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the letters are crazily mixed

explanation.surface: A crank says they love doing this!
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at what the solver is doing with the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving is what a crossword solver does, working out the clue's answer.

clue.text: Able to descry two properties of a needle

parts.note: a needle is sharp at the point
a needle has an eye, so it is eyed

explanation.surface: A needle has two qualities that let it spot things.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen-sighted means spotting things readily, which is what descry means.
